EGLE staffers share favorite Michigan inland lakes for Lakes Appreciation Month
D. T. Crain
Michigan, which has more freshwater shoreline than any other state and 11,000 inland lakes, offers a wide variety of water bodies to residents and visitors. As part of Lakes Appreciation Month, the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) invited its staff members to share their favorite inland lakes.
Some lakes hold special meaning for people due to family traditions or because they are hidden gems that offer enjoyable experiences. EGLE staff highlighted three such lakes in their responses.
Lake Missaukee is one example mentioned by staffers. Located near Lake City, it stands out as a meaningful place for those who visit regularly or have personal connections to the area.
The department's initiative aims to celebrate the state's abundance of freshwater resources and encourage residents to appreciate local natural features during Lakes Appreciation Month.
Further information about Michigan’s many inland lakes and the perspectives shared by EGLE employees can be found on the department’s website.
